paragraphs.text: DSH plugin: monitor DGX Spark temperature & memory usage, set GPU clock.
# dsh-spark-monitor
**English** | 简体中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that puts a live status monitor for **1–4 DGX Spark nodes** at the far rig
ht of the composer status bar, and lets you switch their **GPU clock tiers** from the same button.
Temperature, memory and swap are sampled over SSH (sysfs `hwmon` and `/proc/meminfo`); the clock tie
rs are applied with `sudo -n nvidia-smi -lgc` on every configured node.
## Features
- **Aggregate status pills** — one pill shows the hottest node, one shows the fullest memory; hoveri

ng either lists every node with its own value and sample age.
- **Configurable nodes** — 1 to 4 node

s, each with its own SSH alias, display label, and per-node temperature / memory switches.
- **Confi
gurable clock tiers** — any list of MHz values plus `unlimited`, applied to all nodes from a single

click; the popover highlights the current tier.
- **Per-node failure isolation** — one unreachable n

ode does not break the others; its pill line shows the error.
- **en / zh** dictionaries and a nativ
e settings form in the Desktop plugin manager.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.1-rc.2` (Web UI / Desktop profile).
- Node.js `>= 20` (only for local dev

elopment).
- SSH aliases for every node in `~/.ssh/config`, reachable without a password prompt (`Ba

tchMode=yes`).
- Passwordless sudo on every node for `nvidia-smi` (`sudo -n nvidia-smi ...` must wor

k).
- `nvidia-smi` installed on the nodes (only needed for the clock feature).
### Passwordless sudo (clock feature only)
Sampling temperature and memory needs no privileges. Applying a clock tier runs `sudo -n nvidia-smi
-lgc ...`, so the SSH user needs a NOPASSWD rule:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Replace `your-user` with the SSH user. Without the rule the monitoring pills still work; set `clock:
false` in the config to hide the clock button entirely.
## Install
This package is distributed from GitHub; it is not published to npm.
**Desktop:** open the Plugins page, choose **Add plugin**, and enter `github:zer0kara/dsh-spark-moni
tor` (or the absolute path of a local checkout), then reload the page. The Desktop profile is owned
by the Electron app, so `dsh plugin --profile desktop` is not the way to install there.
**CLI profiles:**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Configuration
The plugin assumes **no host names of its own**: with no `hosts` configured it samples nothing and d
raws nothing in the status bar. Add your nodes in your profile's patch layer (`~/.dsh/profiles/<prof
ile>/cordis.patch.yml`) or in the Desktop plugin-manager form. Replace `node-1` / `node-2` below wit
h the SSH aliases from your own `~/.ssh/config`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| `hosts[].alias` | — (required) | SSH alias from `~/.ssh/config`. Allowed characters: `A-Z a-z 0-9

. _ -`. With no hosts, nothing is sampled. |
| `hosts[].label` | alias | Display label used in toolt

ips. |
| `hosts[].temperature` | `true` | Sample temperatures for this node. |
| `hosts[].memory` |

`true` | Sample memory and swap for this node. |
| `tiers[]` | `1710, 1950, 2190, unlimited` | Clock

tiers offered by the popover. Numbers are MHz; `unlimited` runs `nvidia-smi -rgc`. |
| `clock` | `t
rue` | Enable the GPU clock tier control. Set `false` to hide the clock button when `nvidia-smi` nee

ds a password. |
| `intervalSeconds` | `300` | Host sampling interval (30–86400). |
| `timeoutSecond
s` | `20` | Whole SSH command deadline (5–120). |
The Desktop plugin manager renders the same fields as a form.
## How it works
- **Sampling.** The Host half runs one SSH command per node per interval. It reads `hwmon` `temp*_in
put` files (millidegrees), `/proc/meminfo` (`MemTotal`, `MemAvailable`, `SwapTotal`, `SwapFree`), up
time and load. Each node's snapshot is stored independently; `ageSeconds` is computed by the Host pe

r request.
- **Clock tiers.** Applying a tier runs `sudo -n sh -c 'nvidia-smi -lgc 0,<MHz> && …'` (o
r `-rgc` for `unlimited`) and records the tier in `/var/lib/gpu-clock-lock/tier` on the node. The re
cord file exists because the driver exposes **no query** for the locked clock — only set/reset; the
optional boot service below writes the same file so the pill can show the boot tier after a reboot.
## Optional: persist the clock limit across reboots
`nvidia-smi -lgc` is a runtime setting, so a reboot clears it. The plugin never installs or edits an
y service — this is only a companion example for people who want the limit to survive a reboot.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Replace both `2190` values with your tier. `ExecStartPost` only writes the tier record so the status
pill can show the boot tier (the driver has no query for the locked clock). Without this service th
e plugin still works: the tier applies at runtime, and after a reboot the clocks revert and the pill
shows `—` until you pick a tier again.
## Limitations
- There is no way to read the *actual* locked clock back from the driver; the plugin shows the last
tier it applied (or the boot service's tier). A manual `nvidia-smi -lgc` outside the plugin is invis

ible.
- `nvidia-smi -lgc` does not survive a reboot; use the optional boot service above to persist

it.
- The clock feature needs passwordless sudo; without it the apply fails and the error is shown p

er node.
- SSH aliases must resolve without interactive prompts; use `BatchMode=yes`-friendly keys.
## Development
